newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-OVERMARS, AJAX IDOL AND LOYAL SERVANT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OVERMARS, AJAX IDOL AND LOYAL SERVANT.

text.p: Aged only 23, Marc Overmars has already scaled the dizzy heights of success -- three Dutch championships, the European Cup, the World Club Cup and 30 caps for his country.
But Ajax Amsterdam's diminutive pin-up wants more.

An enforced nine-month lay-off after knee surgery following a collision in a game against De Graafscap last December has given the mercurial winger time to take stock and look ahead at what he wants to achieve in the game.
His injury and lengthy recuperation kept him out of last season's European Cup final against Juventus and, crucially, meant that he missed the Euro 96 summer showcase in England.
At one stage he and Dutch coach Guus Hiddink both hoped for a return in time for the championships but they came too soon.
Overmars turned down Hiddink's invitation to attend the matches -- except the 4-1 Wembley defeat by England -- preferring to watch the tournament on television.
"That wouldn't have been much fun. Once you've played for your country it's not easy to sit in the stands," he said in a recent newspaper interview.
Nor was Overmars over-impressed with the quality of Euro 96. "Too many teams played within themselves. There were far too few attacking games," he reflected.
Despite his injury and not being able to show Europe what he could do, Overmars, always a potential match-winner, continued to attract attention from foreign scouts.
"Even after my operation and aware of the risks of taking on someone with such a serious injury, top foreign clubs expressed their interest in (signing) me," he said.
The winger would ultimately like to ply his trade outside his native Netherlands but remains loyal to Ajax where his contract runs until 2000.
"Sure, I'm ambitious. I had wanted to build a career abroad but things have been so good at Ajax that I put those plans on hold. But I'm still young and there's plenty of time.
"I'm convinced I can make it abroad, even though few teams play with out-and-out wingers. At some point I'll want to be let off the (Ajax) leash."
Overmars joined the Amsterdam club in the summer of 1992 after a season apiece at Go Ahead Eagles and Willem II.
His strengths on the field are his electric pace and excellent close control and he has scored valuable goals for both club and country.
Recently returned to both Ajax and the Dutch national side, Overmars is quickly regaining match fitness and showing signs of his old speed and sharpness.
Come the new millennium, there will be quite a queue building up at Ajax's door, ready to sign up one of the continent's flair performers.
